system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Starting cap of **25% / AUD 6m**. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft; none exists. | **Reject and mark up to AUD 6m** — the proposed fallback is not authorised merely because its number matches the playbook fallback. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** tipping basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore buyer thresholds** — Seller’s proposal materially reduces recovery through both higher thresholds and a deductible basket. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | **24 months** for general claims, confined to that category; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given. | **Reject and require 24 months** — the shorter fallback is unauthorised and must not spill into other claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same general cap and time limit for “administrative simplicity.” | Separate regime: **100% purchase-price cap**, at least **six years**, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject and insert a standalone Fundamental/Title regime** — ownership, capacity and authority risk cannot be diluted by general warranty limitations. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no effective fraud carve-out is offered. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insist on an express comprehensive carve-out** — this is a non-waivable buyer position. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Deems the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records generally disclosed, alongside specific disclosures. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Delete general disclosures 1.1–1.2 and retain only qualifying specific disclosures** — document availability alone does not fairly disclose warranty exceptions. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; any seller-knowledge qualifier should identify named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 as drafted** — it improperly converts constructive and adviser knowledge into a broad warranty defence. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | Effective Bluefen consent **and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Strengthen the condition precedent and prohibit consent-on-delivery satisfaction** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and reasonable endeavours do not remove the material risk. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release will follow Completion. | Current payout statement, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. Any later release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require payout and simultaneous releases at Completion** — no authority exists to accept unsecured post-Completion delivery risk. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | Treats the **AUD 420,000** bonuses as a Seller matter but omits them from the funds flow; on-costs are unaddressed. | Express seller funding or a specific funds-flow line for AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Add an explicit seller-funded completion item and quantify on-costs** — omission creates a risk that the Company bears an undisclosed completion liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; relies on an unverified **AUD 180,000** open amount. | Broader indemnity covering losses arising from non-payment and failure of ownership, transfer or assignment of SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving a cure through verified payment and confirmatory transfer. | **Broaden the indemnity and require evidence of cure** — paying an unverified sum alone does not establish that the Company owns the relevant IP. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Describes DD-006 as preliminary and not expected to be material; no confirmed access, breach, notification duty or loss is established. | Preserve logs and evidence, complete a documented investigation, provide continuing updates and comply with any substantiated remediation or notification obligations, without assuming a breach or numeric claim. | **Impose preservation, investigation and update covenants while reserving rights** — the facts remain unresolved and should not be prematurely minimised or overstated. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Characterises three **AUD 110,000** renewals—AUD 330,000 total—as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, termination rights, accrual, scope and ordinary-course status; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Reserve classification pending diligence** — the disclosure itself does not establish that the renewals are unavoidable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Proposes that limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded and treats Tax/IP as governed by the general regime. | Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, without a hidden general-regime override. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture by claim category** — a global “all Claims” provision could unintentionally override specifically negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on the internal DD-012 share register as evidence that Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, authority and absence/release of encumbrances, including appropriate corporate and security searches and completion deliverables. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive proof** — a supplied internal register identifies the asserted holder but is not independent title or encumbrance verification. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Says Tax and IP warranties are settled under the proposed general regime. | Keep both regimes expressly **open** pending substantive negotiation; do not assume unlimited liability or any agreed cap, period or allocation. | **Reject the assertion of settlement and reserve all Tax/IP terms** — no buyer-authorised resolution exists, and Seller’s characterisation cannot create one. |
=== END ADVICE ===
